Thought: To determine which compound has the highest boiling point, I need to analyze the intermolecular forces present in each compound. Boiling points are influenced by the strength of these intermolecular forces: stronger forces lead to higher boiling points. I will consider the types of intermolecular forces (dispersion forces, dipole-dipole interactions, and hydrogen bonding) for each compound.

- 2-methylbutane, 2-methylpropane, and butane are all hydrocarbons, so they primarily exhibit dispersion forces (also known as London dispersion forces). These forces are generally weaker than dipole-dipole interactions and hydrogen bonding.
- Dimethyl ether (CH3OCH3) is an ether and has a polar C-O bond, which means it can exhibit dipole-dipole interactions in addition to dispersion forces.

Since dipole-dipole interactions are generally stronger than dispersion forces alone, dimethyl ether is expected to have a higher boiling point than the hydrocarbons listed.
